statement: Seven hazard domains are specified. Selected claims in each specification were reviewed against saved primary sources: what a source supports is marked, and what no source supports is held back and not used. None of the seven runs in the Aegis engine yet: the code holds only the general resource-shortfall formulation. The public haze guidance page runs on sourced cards.

domains.name: Seismic
domains.hazard: Earthquakes: shaking intensity, damaged shelter and injured people.

audit.text: The Modified Mercalli scale runs I to XII (USGS Circular 1045); water at 15 litres per person per day matches the Sphere Handbook.

An exact ground-acceleration equivalent for an intensity level is not a property of the scale (USGS calls it an arbitrary ranking of observed effects); the acceleration bands rest on Italian zone rules.

domains.name: Hydrological
domains.hazard: Floods: water depth and flow, unsafe water and displaced households.

audit.text: The Sphere 15-litre daily minimum is confirmed, with its stated context cases (7.5 litres in acute drought, 50 in urban settings).
A coping-capacity scale of 0.1 to 1.0 conflicts with the published 0 to 10 scale of the INFORM risk report; the water-kit denominators and the composite index have no source.
Several items rest on a flood-forecasting document that was not read, so they stay unverified.

domains.name: Meteorological
domains.hazard: Cyclones and severe storms: wind, storm surge and lost shelter.

audit.text: The dynamic-pressure formula, the knots conversion and the wind cut-offs of 64, 83, 96 and 113 knots match saved NOAA and NHC sources.

Storm-surge heights of 2.0, 2.5 and 4.0 m cannot be derived from the category (NHC says surge depends on storm size, track and coast); the gust thresholds are not a feature of any saved source, and central pressure is no longer a criterion of the scale.

domains.name: Wildfire
domains.hazard: Wildfires and the smoke that follows, including regional haze.

audit.text: Fire radiative power is reported in megawatts (NASA FIRMS product description).
The spread equation, its coefficients, the distance and time tiers and the population gate are not on the NASA page that was read; this is an absence on one page, not a search of all literature.

domains.name: Biological
domains.hazard: Disease outbreaks: how fast an infection spreads and what care and protection is needed.
domains.inputFeeds: WHO Disease Outbreak News / CDC feeds

audit.text: The definitions of the basic reproduction number and of the duration of infectiousness match the WHO Unity study protocol.

The numeric ranges, the hospitalisation ratio of 0.15 and most other constants are not in that protocol, which gives no operational thresholds; the water formula conflicts with the Sphere 15-litre minimum.

domains.name: Displacement
domains.hazard: People displaced into camps or settlements: space, sanitation, water and nutrition.

audit.text: 45 square metres per person and the latrine ratios (1 per 20 people in the medium term, 1 per 50 in the first phase) are in the Sphere Handbook; an acute-malnutrition prevalence of 15 to 29.9 percent (weight-for-height) is the IPC critical band.
Sphere gives 30 square metres only where communal services are outside the settlement, so it cannot be called an absolute minimum; the influx and access-index triggers have no source.

domains.specFile: 0007_EG-FRM-007_domain-7-volcanic-formulation-and-sop.md (the file name says Domain 7; its content is Domain 6)

domains.name: Volcanic
domains.hazard: Eruptions and ashfall: roof loads, breathing hazards and clean-up.

audit.text: A source says roof collapse typically needs ash thicker than 100 mm, but non-engineered, long-span and low-pitched roofs may collapse at about 100 mm or less; the roof-load formula is dimensionally consistent, but its equation was an image missing from the saved page.
The 5 mm and 50 mm cut-offs, the plume-radius constants, the vent-distance decay and the 10 km zone are not in the saved sources; the volcanic explosivity index page could not be read.
